lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the sticky glandular herb + bilabiate flower + woody two-horned capsule as a highly memorable Lamiales fruit architecture.

project_scope.note: The sole project species is accepted and native in Texas under current Kew; strict project county-range approval remains species-level.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the sticky glandular herbage, then the large bilateral tubular flower. Confirm a superior 2-carpellate ovary and the extraordinary fruit whose woody endocarp splits into two long curved horns.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual or perennial herbs, often sprawling; leaves commonly opposite and broad; stems and leaves often densely covered with sticky glandular trichomes.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and strongly zygomorphic with a fused 5-lobed corolla; commonly 4 fertile stamens plus a staminode; ovary superior and 2-carpellate.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A fleshy developing capsule whose outer tissues are shed at maturity, leaving a hard woody capsule/endocarp with a long beak splitting into two hooklike horns.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Sticky glandular plant + big bilabiate flower + devil's-claw two-horned fruit = Martyniaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: glandular hairs → bilabiate flower → 4 stamens + staminode → developing fruit → two-horned woody capsule
visual_lesson.intro: Martyniaceae is a fruit-first family. Once you see the mature devil's claw, the rest of the plant becomes much easier to place.

steps.title: 1 · See the sticky glandular hairs
steps.look_for: Dense glandular hairs coating the leaves and stems with sticky secretions.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a strong whole-plant clue before fruit develops.

steps.title: 2 · Read the bilabiate flower
steps.look_for: Large fused 5-lobed corolla with obvious bilateral symmetry and nectar-guide markings.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows the underlying Lamiales flower architecture.

steps.title: 3 · Count 4 fertile stamens + staminode
steps.look_for: Four functional stamens and one reduced sterile staminode.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the flower to several Lamiales relatives while fruit provides the family-level finish.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the fruit into the devil's claw
steps.photo_role: green fruit → dry woody endocarp sequence
steps.look_for: A long-beaked fruit; as the fleshy outer layer disappears, the hardened beak splits into two curved horns.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the most unmistakable fruit transformations in the local flora.

comparisons.title: Martyniaceae vs Bignoniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Lamiales with showy bilateral flowers. Martyniaceae is a sticky glandular herb with a heavy two-horned woody capsule; Bignoniaceae commonly has woody vines/trees and long bivalved capsules with flat winged seeds.

comparisons.title: Martyniaceae vs Datura
comparisons.rule: Both can be coarse sticky herbs with large tubular flowers and conspicuous capsules, but Datura is Solanaceae with radial/funnel flowers and a prickly capsule rather than a beaked two-horned devil's claw.

visual_lesson.caveat: The sticky hairs are useful but not sufficient by themselves. Confirm the distinctive fruit whenever available.

genera.fast_cue: sticky glandular herb + large bilabiate flower + long-beaked fruit splitting into two horns

visual_targets.structure: green fruit to two-horned mature capsule
visual_targets.annotation_goal: show fleshy outer layer loss and horn split
